title: Termination of the circuit walk
statement: Let $C$ be a family of directed acyclic circuits, and suppose the circuit for input length $n$ is canonical: each gate's argument list is strictly increasing, and its output vertex is the last vertex. For any Boolean parameter $\ell$ and natural number $i$, the walk on the paired encoding of the unary word $1^n$ and the binary representation of $i$, started in its start state with all four registers zero and no answer yet, eventually halts with answer $\ell\lor b$ if $i$ is less than the circuit's encoding length, where $b$ is bit $i$ of that encoding (taking a missing bit to be false); otherwise it halts with answer false. At every time strictly before it halts, each register is at most the length of the circuit encoding.
hypotheses_covered: the circuit for length $n$ is canonical
initial state is start, registers are zero, and answer is unset
